title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, contractors and consultants of the Company and its subsidiaries. Bound only by the general principles (insider trading, conflicts, no personal advantage from non-public information); the Prohibited Period, Notification, hedging and short-term/short-selling restrictions apply only to Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Any person with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company (including any director), any employee invited to participate in the Executive and Senior Staff Incentive Plan, and anyone notified by the Company that they are a Designated Person. Subject to Prohibited Periods, prior Notification, the hedging ban and the short-term dealing and short-selling bans.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Sub-tier of Designated Persons distinguished only for the Notification regime (Notification to the Chair of the Audit Committee and Company Secretary; Prohibited Period consent from the Chair of the Audit Committee).

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chairman; distinguished for the Notification regime (Notification to the Chairman and Company Secretary, post-trade written notice to the Company Secretary) and for Listing Rule 3.19A relevant-interest notifications.

tiers.name: Other Designated Persons
tiers.description: Designated Persons other than the Chairman and directors; distinguished only for the Notification regime (Notification to the Company Secretary, no post-trade notice).

tiers.name: Related Parties
tiers.description: Each immediate family member of a Person and each company, trust or entity controlled by the Person or an immediate family member. A Designated Person must take all reasonable and necessary steps to prevent Related Party dealing unless the Designated Person has complied with the Policy on the Related Party's behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in Company Securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may declare other blackout periods from time to time; these form part of the Prohibited Period. The Policy is silent on whether such blackouts are confidential or how they are communicated.

rules.detail: No standalone derivatives rule for vested, unlocked shares. Company Securities include derivatives and other financial products created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, and dealing includes buying or selling them or agreeing to do so, and any transaction limiting economic risk of a holding. An OTC put and call with a bank is therefore a dealing requiring prior Notification, execution within 7 days, and is barred during Prohibited Periods and while holding inside information.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products created by the Company or created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures, options or other securities able to be traded on ASX or another stock exchange

rules.detail: Acquiring derivatives or options in relation to Company Securities that hedge or transfer the risk of fluctuation in value of an unvested entitlement (including equity rights subject to time and/or performance hurdles) is expressly banned.
rules.evidence: This would include acquiring derivatives or options in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: The same express ban on acquiring derivatives or options extends to Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock. This would include acquiring derivatives or options in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Persons who are not Designated Persons are bound only by the general principles (insider trading, conflicts, no personal advantage from non-public information); the Notification, Prohibited Period and hedging restrictions are not applied to them.
rules.evidence: Persons who possess "inside information" must not deal or procure dealing in Company Securities

rules.detail: Absolute ban on transactions having the effect of hedging or transferring the risk of fluctuation in value of any unvested entitlement, including equity rights subject to time and/or performance hurdles. No approval route.
rules.evidence: A Designated Person must not enter into transactions which would have the effect of hedging or transferring the risk of any fluctuation in the value of: (a) any unvested entitlement to Company Securities

rules.detail: Vested securities still subject to a holding lock cannot be hedged; a collar over holding-locked plan shares is prohibited until the lock lifts.
rules.evidence: (b) Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The hedging ban is confined to unvested and holding-locked securities. Hedging vested, unlocked shares is a dealing (agreements or transactions limiting economic risk of a holding) and so is permitted subject to prior Notification, the 7-day execution window, Prohibited Periods and the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in Company Securities.

rules.detail: The hedging ban is addressed to Designated Persons only; other Persons remain subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: A Designated Person must not enter into transactions which would have the effect of hedging

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (collars, prepaid forwards, equity swaps) are not named. They would be caught only as economic-risk-limiting dealings and, if over unvested or holding-locked securities, by the hedging ban.
Outright ban on short selling Company Securities, expressed to apply notwithstanding any other provision of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Notwithstanding any provision in this Policy, a Designated Person must not: ... (b) short sell Company Securities

rules.detail: Designated Persons must not knowingly allow their Company Securities to be used for short selling, which captures lending shares into a short-selling programme. Lending for other purposes is not addressed and is not a dealing under the definition.
rules.evidence: (c) knowingly allow their Company Securities to be used for short selling.

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. They are financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares and so a dealing requiring Notification, but a short CFD would breach the short-selling ban and a CFD opened and closed within 3 months would be Short Term Dealing.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products created by the Company or created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares

rules.detail: Margin loans are not mentioned anywhere in the Policy; there is no ban, notification or forced-sale provision.
Granting a charge, lien, pledge or other security over Company Securities is not mentioned and is not within the dealing definition.

No provision on borrowing against Company Securities. The loan leg of a funded collar is unregulated by the Policy, though a lender's enforcement sale would be a disposal by the Designated Person with no forced-sale carve-out.

Ban on Short Term Dealing, defined as dealing in Company Securities within a 3 month period. Carve-out for sale of securities acquired by conversion (e.g. exercise of an option) or in accordance with the Executive and Senior Staff Incentive Plan or other Company incentive scheme.
rules.evidence: Short Term Dealing includes dealing in Company Securities within a 3 month period, but does not include the sale of Company Securities after they have been acquired through the conversion of a security, for example the exercise of an option, or in accordance with the Executive and Senior Staff Incentive Plan or other Company incentive scheme.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit Committee and the Company Secretary (Notification only, no approval); prior written consent of the Chair of the Audit Committee for a Prohibited Period disposal
clearance.evidence: The Chairman must not deal in Company Securities without first submitting a Notification to the Chair of the Audit Committee and the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction and must trade within seven days of submitting the Notification. The Chairman must subsequently notify the Company Secretary in writing of any trade that has occurred.

clearance.approver: Chairman and the Company Secretary (Notification only, no approval); prior written consent of the Chairman for a Prohibited Period disposal
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('subsequently notify'); Listing Rule 3.19A notice as soon as possible and in time for lodgement within 5 business days
clearance.evidence: Directors (other than the Chairman) must not deal in Company Securities without first submitting a Notification to the Chairman and the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction and must trade within seven days of submitting the Notification. The director must subsequently notify the Company Secretary in writing of any trade that has occurred.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (Notification only, no approval); prior written consent of the Chairman for a Prohibited Period disposal
clearance.evidence: Designated Persons other than the Chairman and directors must not deal in Company Securities without first submitting a Notification to the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction and must trade within seven days of the Notification.
Persons who possess "inside information" must not deal or procure dealing in Company Securities

short_term.basis: dealing within a 3 month period (reference point not specified)
carve_outs: sale of Company Securities acquired through the conversion of a security, for example the exercise of an option
sale in accordance with the Executive and Senior Staff Incentive Plan or other Company incentive scheme
short_term.evidence: Short Term Dealing includes dealing in Company Securities within a 3 month period

exceptions.evidence: may be given written clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of (but not purchase) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period, where the Designated Person is in severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Chairman (Chair of the Audit Committee for the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: is required by law to transfer the Company Securities

exceptions.approver: Chairman (Chair of the Audit Committee for the Chairman)
exceptions.evidence: or where other exceptional circumstances exist. Where clearance is given, the Designated Person must trade the Company Securities within 7 days of receiving clearance.

subscribe for securities offered under a disclosure document (e.g. a prospectus); ... acquire Company Securities under a bonus issue, rights issue or other offer made to all holders of securities of the same class; acquire Company Securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan

acquire, or agree to acquire, options under a Company share option plan; acquire, or agree to acquire, rights under a Company performance share plan; exercise options acquired under a Company share option plan (but may not sell all or part of the shares received upon exercise of the options other than in accordance with these procedures)

external_documents: Executive and Senior Staff Incentive Plan (referenced for the Designated Person definition, the Short Term Dealing carve-out and holding locks)
exemption_authority: Chairman (or, for the Chairman, the Chair of the Audit Committee) may give written clearance for a Designated Person not holding inside information to sell or otherwise dispose of (but not purchase) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period on demonstrated severe financial hardship, legal requirement to transfer, or other exceptional circumstances; the trade must occur within 7 days. No authority to waive the hedging, short-term dealing or short-selling bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person must not enter into transactions which would have the effect of hedging or transferring the risk of any fluctuation in the value of ... Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collared shares must be both vested and free of any plan holding lock; the bank should verify the lock status of each parcel before inception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: To deal and dealing includes ... entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar is a dealing in its own right regardless of venue or whether the OTC options are 'Company Securities', so Notification, the 7-day execution window and Prohibited Periods apply to inception, roll and unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives and other financial products created by the Company or created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures, options or other securities able to be traded on ASX or another stock exchange
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'able to be traded on ASX' qualifier could be read as limiting derivatives to exchange-traded products, but the economic-risk limb of dealing captures an OTC collar in any event.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Notification means a notification in writing (including by email) that includes ... a confirmation that the Designated Person is not in possession of price sensitive information about the Company that is not generally available to the market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Prohibited Periods no one approves the dealing; the executive self-certifies and must execute within seven days of the Notification, so the collar must be priced and signed inside that window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Season means each of: (a) the period from the end of the financial year or half financial year to the business day after the time of release of the annual or half year results; and (b) the period from the end of the September quarter or March quarter to the business day after the time of release of the September or March quarterly reports.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly reporting produces four closed seasons per year plus Board blackouts, narrowing the windows for inception, roll, unwind and physical settlement of the collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: prohibited period relief is disposal only
bespoke_clauses.clause: may be given written clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of (but not purchase) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Buying back the written call or purchasing a put to unwind or restructure during a Prohibited Period cannot be cleared even in hardship; only a disposal (e.g. delivery of shares on call exercise) could be.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must refrain from dealing in Company Securities during Prohibited Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for a lender's enforcement sale or for physical settlement at expiry, so a bank enforcing its security or exercising the call in a Closed Season could put the Designated Person in breach; expiry dates and enforcement mechanics should avoid Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short Term Dealing includes dealing in Company Securities within a 3 month period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with a tenor under three months, or an unwind within three months of inception, risks characterisation as Short Term Dealing; tenor should exceed three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Designated Person may not deal in Company Securities, he or she must take all reasonable and necessary steps to prevent any dealing in Company Securities by Related Parties unless the Designated Person has complied with this Policy on behalf of that Related Party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or controlled company requires the Designated Person to make the Notification on the Related Party's behalf and observe Prohibited Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A director is required to notify the Company Secretary if there is any change in the director's relevant interest in securities of the Company ... with sufficient notice to allow the Company Secretary to make the necessary notifications within 5 business days after the change occurs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and the security granted to the bank will be disclosed to ASX via Appendix 3Y, so the arrangement will be public within five business days.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unlocked shares is possible for Fortescue directors and executives under this policy. The put and call are a dealing (via the economic-risk limb of the dealing definition and the inclusion of third-party derivatives in Company Securities) and so require a prior written Notification (to the Chair of the Audit Committee and Company Secretary for the Chairman, the Chairman and Company Secretary for other directors, and the Company Secretary for other Designated Persons), execution within seven days, and must fall outside the four Closed Seasons and any Board blackout and not while holding inside information. Hedging of unvested entitlements and of vested shares still subject to a holding lock is absolutely prohibited. The loan and the security over the collared shares are not addressed at all: there is no margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing restriction and no disclosure requirement, but equally no forced-sale carve-out, and Prohibited Period clearance is discretionary and disposal-only, so settlement, enforcement and unwind mechanics should be timed to avoid Prohibited Periods and the collar tenor should exceed three months to avoid the Short Term Dealing ban.
